stem: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral whose diagonals intersect at $F$. $X \in \overline{AF}$ and $Y \in \overline{DF}$ such that $\overline{XY} \parallel \overline{AD}$. Given $m(\angle CAD) = {=a}^\circ$ and $m(\angle XBC) = {=b}^\circ$, prove that $BXYC$ is a cyclic quadrilateral and find $m(\angle XCY)$ in degrees.
solution: $m(\angle CBD) = m(\angle CAD) = {=a}^\circ$ (inscribed angles on the same arc $CD$).
So $m(\angle CXY) = m(\angle CBY) = {=a}^\circ$, two angles on the base $\overline{CY}$ and in one direction of it, hence $BXYC$ is cyclic.
$m(\angle XBY) = m(\angle XBC) - m(\angle CBD) = {=b} - {=a} = {=b - a}^\circ$.
In the cyclic quadrilateral $BXYC$, $m(\angle XCY) = m(\angle XBY)$ (inscribed on the same arc $XY$), so it equals ${=b - a}^\circ$.
notes: Standard: parallel lines give equal angles, then cyclic, then equal inscribed angles. b>a keeps the configuration valid (diagonal BY lies inside angle XBC).
